title: GitHub Trending Today #11: SyncKit, RepoMind, Vex, runprompt, Markdown Viewer, beads_viewer, Pulse

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Today's episode is GitHub trending today number 11. We've got 25 hot projects that developers across the world are starring and forking right now. Let's dive into the repositories lighting up GitHub today. Let's go.

sections.title: SyncKit
paragraphs: First up, SyncKit, a sync engine for building realtime collaborative applications. If you've ever tried building Sync yourself, you know the pain. It takes months. It's fragile. And existing tools are either too complex, too expensive, or not truly offline. Synkit fixes all of that. With just three lines of code, you get productionready syncing, complete offline support, and real-time updates, all wrapped inside a tiny 59 kilob bundle.

sections.title: RepoMind
paragraphs: Repind. And if you've ever wished you could talk to a GitHub repo instead of digging through thousands of lines of code, this tool is going to blow your mind. Repo Mind is AI powered agentic CAG platform that lets you chat with any public repo or GitHub profile. No cloning, no permissions, no setup. Just paste a URL and start asking questions.

sections.title: Vex
paragraphs: Vex, a beautiful Excel and CSV viewer built in Go. Yep, Excel in your terminal, but actually gorgeous. Pick from six stunning themes. Cat Pooin, Nord, Rosé Pine, Tokyo Knight, Groove Box, even Dracula. navigation, smooth, vim keys, arrow keys, global search, and fast sheet switching. Copy cells, export to CSV or JSON, toggle formulas, all without leaving the terminal.

sections.title: runprompt
paragraphs: Runrompt, the no friction tool for anyone who builds with prompt files. Runrompt is a single file Python script that executes.prompt files, those handy executable prompt templates that pack the prompt, model config, and metadata into one neat file. No installs, no virtual M's, no dependency headaches. Just drop the script in your project and run your prompts.

sections.title: Markdown Viewer
paragraphs: Markdown Viewer, the tool that finally ends the ritual of wrestling your Markdown into a perfect Word doc. If you love writing in Markdown, but dread the export, messy formulas, lowres diagrams, fiddly tables, and one more hour of formatting, this one's for you. Markdown Viewer turns your markdown into publication ready Word with a single click. and it does it locally and for free. Beads viewer or simply BV, a fast keyboard-driven terminal interface for the beads issue tracker. If you live in

sections.title: beads_viewer
paragraphs: your terminal and love tools that move at the speed of thought, this one's going to feel like home. BV is all about focus, speed, and clarity. Instead of fighting through laggy web dashboards, you get instant offline browsing of thousands of issues, all navigated with familiar Vim style keys.

sections.title: Doraemon Paper Comicizer
paragraphs: Next is Doromon Paper Comicizer. Imagine taking a dense, brainmelting academic PDF and turning it into a friendly kidstyle Doramon comic. That's exactly what this tool does, powered by Gemini 3 Pro. You upload any academic paper and you watch it unfold in real time. Each page appears instantly in a clean comic viewer with full-size previews, thumbnails, and smooth navigation.

sections.title: Pulse
paragraphs: Pulse, a digital experience platform built to show you exactly how users interact with your product in real time. If you're running a large app, a micros service stack, or anything customerf facing, Pulse gives you the kind of visibility that turns guesswork into precision. Pulse fuses behavioral and business analytics into a single live dashboard so you can understand not just what users are doing.

sections.title: Claude Usage Tracker
paragraphs: Claude Usage Tracker, a native Mac OS menu bar app that gives you real-time insight into your Claude code API usage. If you've ever struggled to keep track of AI API costs across projects, this little utility is a gamecher. Automatic silent updates, one-click release notes, CSV export, configurable pricing per model, and even multi- language and currency support. Imagine an AI that can take multiple images and turn them into a coherent dynamic visual universe.

sections.title: iMontage
paragraphs: That's eye montage. It's like giving your images video like motion prior. So even separate images feel connected and fluid. Whether you're combining pictures, following detailed instructions, or creating complex multi-image outputs, I montage keeps everything consistent and stunning.

sections.title: MinerU-HTML
paragraphs: Minor UHTML, an advanced tool for extracting the main content from HTML pages using the power of large language models. If you've ever struggled with messy web pages full of ads, navigation bars, or side content, Minor UHTML is built to deliver clean, structured HTML bodies, perfect for deep research agents, rag applications, or training data set generation.

sections.title: Web3 Decoder
paragraphs: Ever struggled analyzing blockchain calls directly in Burp Suite? Meet Web3 decoder, the ultimate burp extension for Ethereum and compatible networks like Polygon, Arbitum, BSC, and more. It decodes ETH call and fend raw transaction JSON RPC calls, even the inner functions, letting you see exactly what's happening under the hood.

sections.title: podcast-server
paragraphs: Sick of podcast ads ruining your vibe? Say hello to the podcast ad removal server. It transcribes your episodes with whisper, then uses Claude to spot every ad segment. FFmpeg cleans the audio, cutting out ads and keeping everything in sync. Every episode streams through a modified RSS feed. Works with any podcast app. Self-hosted personal use only.

sections.title: Voxel4D
paragraphs: Voxal 4D, a framework for vision ccentric 4D spatial forecasting and planning. Tailored for autonomous driving. This project is designed to work reliably across all conditions, rain, snow, nighttime, making it a robust solution for realworld driving scenarios. Voxal 4D combines vision highfidelity 4D predictions enabling safer and smarter autonomous driving

sections.title: LatentMAS
paragraphs: latent mass. It's a multi-agent reasoning framework that moves agent collaboration from text into the model's latent space. Instead of long clunky reasoning traces, agents share latent thoughts directly through working memory. Super fast and efficient. Key perks, fewer tokens, training free alignment, and it works with any hugging face model, plus optional VLM backends.

sections.title: DSpico Hardware
paragraphs: Ever wanted to build your own Nintendo DS flash cart? Meet Despico, the fully open source DS flash cart. Everything's open, PCB, shell, stickers, even the box art. You can DIY it yourself or have it manufactured. It's powered by an RP2040 microcontroller, has 16 megabit flash, a micro SD slot, dual power support, and even two LEDs for style.

sections.title: FastRL
paragraphs: Fast RL, the high efficiency reinforcement learning framework for language models. It crushes the longtail rollout bottleneck with adaptive speculative decoding, keeping every roll out mathematically lossless. Need speed? Its adaptive rollout engine automatically optimizes strategies while its drafter training makes sure your GPU cycles are never wasted.

sections.title: SteadyDancer
paragraphs: Steady Dancer, the human image animation framework that preserves the first frame while generating smooth, coherent motion. Unlike older reference to video methods that lose identity or introduce visual glitches, Steady Dancer's imagetovideo approach ensures harmonized motion with precise control. It uses a condition reconciliation mechanism to balance fidelity and motion.

sections.title: Go Memory Layout Visualizer
paragraphs: Go memory layout visualizer, a VS Code extension that shows you every bite, alignment, and cache line in real time. See padding waste, field offsets, and nested strrus instantly, and optimize your strrus with just one click. Reduce memory usage by up to 30% and boost cache performance without changing a single line of logic.

sections.title: Darwin
paragraphs: Darwin, the enterprisegrade ML platform that handles it all. From distributed training and feature engineering to experiment tracking and real-time model serving, Darwin's got you covered. Scale effortlessly with Kubernetes and Ray. Optimize costs with autoscaling and spot instances. And deploy models in minutes, not days. With SDK first design, it's production ready and developer friendly.

sections.title: Urlvy
paragraphs: Orvi, your smart link shortener with a twist. Turn URLs into clean branded slugs. Get AI powered summaries and track every click live. See where your traffic comes from, which devices are popular, and even chat with Earl Statsbot to ask why clicks spiked yesterday. Set links to auto expire, pause anytime, and manage your traffic from a sleek dashboard.

sections.title: Sip
paragraphs: SIP, the cozy, serene new tab page that makes every click feel like a mini vacation. Choose from gorgeous cat puchin themes, mocha for dark mode or latte for light, and enjoy stunning glass morphism effects with ambient glows. Quickly search across Google, GitHub, or YouTube. Check the weather, see dynamic greetings, and even get a random inspirational quote to brighten your day.

sections.title: Agent Commands
paragraphs: Level up your AI workflow with agent commands. This is a treasure trove of readytouse commands and skills for Claude. From global commands you can reuse across projects to specific ones tuned for particular tasks. Want Claude to browse the web or control your terminal? Skills for Puppeteer and T-Mux make it happen. Driving your browser or CLI directly with keystrokes and scraped output.

sections.title: dns-honeypot
paragraphs: Ever wondered what the internet would do if you just listened? Meet DNS Honeypot. Spin up a DNS resolver on a clean IP that nobody advertises and let the world talk to it. No replies, no tricks, just logging everything with Unbound, Loki, Prometheus, Graphana, and Trey. Captured live queries, top clients, popular domains, and traffic spikes in real time.

sections.title: Smoothify
paragraphs: Got jagged, pixelated polygons from your raster data. Meet Smoothify. This Python package takes your rough raster to vector geometries and turns them into smooth, clean, and visually appealing shapes using an optimized Chakens corner cutting algorithm. Smoothify keeps the shape and area intact, works with all geometry types, even ones with holes, and handles large data sets efficiently with multipprocessing.
